target_customer: Regulated operations teams in banking, fraud and risk, and law enforcement; originally software developers
problem: Regulated workflows such as fraud review and reconciliation take days. Patched executes them in hours with audit trails, human approvals and policy enforcement. Originally it automated code review and patching.
business_model: Volume based enterprise pricing, with SLA ownership of outcomes
product_category: AI workflow execution for regulated operations (earlier open source developer workflow automation)

founders.name: Rohan Sood
education: Master's in optimization algorithms, NTU Singapore (per YC page)
previous_startups: Earlier company acquired in 2023 (acquirer not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page cites a million dollar CSA Innovation Award from the Singapore government.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining deterministic workflow orchestration with AI reasoning and air gapped deployment for banks is real enterprise engineering on commodity models.

defensibility.rationale: The open source code review phase was easily copied, and the regulated ops phase relies on enterprise integrations and SLA ownership that may build stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A Product Hunt commenter said the original product was uncannily similar to another tool. The company later moved away from developer tools to regulated operations.

market_need_then: In 2024 AI code review and patching tools were crowded; later the company targeted regulated operations where it reports 30 thousand to 2 million items processed monthly by customers, which is a self reported claim.

branding.domain_note: Uses patched.codes, a .codes domain tied to the developer phase, while the regulated ops product kept the same domain.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and compliance oriented, execution over orchestration

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt on 11 September 2024, hunted by Michael Seibel, with 255 upvotes and rank 6 for the day; open source patchwork library on GitHub.

brand_strength.rationale: A past tense verb that fits patching code but not regulated operations, and the .codes domain reflects the earlier developer focus. Some developer awareness from the Product Hunt launch.

pivots.from: Open source AI workflow automation for developers (code review, patching, docs via patchwork)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; the date is approximate and inferred from two separate YC launch posts.

outcome_analysis: Patched is active but its story is unclear. It launched open source developer workflow tools in September 2024, then repositioned to AI for regulated operations and now cites customers in fraud, banking and reconciliation. Company site lists Y Combinator, IQT and SG Innovate as backers but no amounts or dates were found, so funding stays unknown and no success or failure verdict is supported.
notes: Company site says backed by Y Combinator, IQT and SG Innovate; no round amount or date was found in four searches. CB Insights shows an undisclosed pre seed dated 25 September 2024; one CB Insights page describes a different Patched (IT support automation) so it was not used. Asankhaya Sharma is described as CTO and co-founder by a CB Insights news snippet, but the YC page lists only Rohan Sood as founder, so Sharma is not listed. Patchwork on GitHub is licensed AGPL-3.0. Prior employers and the acquirer of Rohan's earlier company not found.
